chapter: Apollo years, Eubie Blake and failing eyesight
title: Copying for Russell Wooding at the Riviera
summary: Whaley copied music for arranger Russell Wooding's show at the Riviera across the Hudson, and recalls how Wooding died in a fire.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: That's where Russell Wooding, we went over there on May 15th and ice and snow and we -- he arranged and I copied.
Russell Wooding. A show over there.
It was over on the banks of the Hudson.
Across the river, yeah. Palisades Park over there.
And you put on a show over there.
Yeah, we went there in the dead of winter like. We was all in our overcoats working and they had heaters going on and we were arranging the music. Russell Wooding.
What did Russell do, did he play piano too.
He was an arranger. He was from Washington, D. C.
How you say he died, he got burned up.
Smoking a pipe, or smoking something and went to sleep. Burnt up.
This was over at the Riveria, you ought to tell me about that. What year was that, Tom.
Gee, I forget. Let me see, it must have been around '33 or '4.
Earlier than that, maybe because Paul Whiteman was over there in '33.
Well, it was right during that big age. They closed one season and opened another and they had -- Russell had the job, so I went over there with him and copied music. We on.
